speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you have been experiencing persistent bleeding after your wisdom tooth extraction and a history of easy bruising; could you please describe exactly how the bleeding is occurring and how long it has lasted?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient was brought in by his mother for persistent bleeding following elective removal of wisdom teeth. The bleeding from the surrounding gums was minimally responsive to multiple gauze packs. The patient also has a history of easy bruising. Family history includes the patient's uncle who had similar issues with bleeding and a history of easy bruising and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is concerning; given your family history of bleeding and joint swelling, could you tell me if you have experienced frequent nosebleeds or heavy menstrual bleeding in female relatives? Also, do you notice bleeding from your gums or skin when you brush your teeth or get minor bumps?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Persistent bleeding from gums following tooth extraction. I also have History of easy bruising, Family history of similar bleeding problems and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Hemophilia A (Factor VIII deficiency) or Hemophilia B (Factor IX deficiency).

Given your family history of joint swelling and bleeding tendencies in male relatives, this strongly suggests an X-linked recessive bleeding disorder. Have you ever had spontaneous bleeding into your joints (hemarthrosis), such as in your knees or elbows?
